messages.content: I need to start planning Chicago for the installation. The cases are due at the museum Monday afternoon, October 20. I can fly from Atlanta Sunday evening or very early Monday, and I expect to come back Thursday, October 23, but the lender has not confirmed when the handoff will finish.

I can compare both outbound windows and keep the Thursday return flexible. What time do you need to be at the museum Monday, and should I limit the search to nonstop flights into O'Hare, or include Midway as well?
I need to be there by noon, before the cases arrive around 1:30. Nonstop only. O'Hare is more practical for this job, so use that.

For Sunday, the two useful nonstop choices are a 6:10 p.m. departure arriving at O'Hare at 7:20 p.m. local time and a 7:35 p.m. departure arriving at 8:45 p.m. The Monday options that still allow a noon museum arrival leave Atlanta at 6:00 a.m. and 7:10 a.m., arriving at 7:10 and 8:20. Ground travel from O'Hare to the museum can run 45 to 75 minutes on a weekday morning, so both Monday flights work on paper, but they leave much less room for a delay.
What are the fares if we pair each one with a reasonable Thursday evening return? I do not want to choose the return too early until I know the handoff schedule.

Using a 7:05 p.m. Thursday return as a comparison point, the Sunday 6:10 p.m. outbound is $428 round trip, and the Sunday 7:35 p.m. option is $401. The Monday 6:00 a.m. pairing is $389, while the 7:10 a.m. pairing is $376. All four are standard economy fares that permit changes, though any fare difference would apply. The lowest restrictive fares are about $45 less, but they are a poor fit while Thursday remains uncertain.
Agreed. I am not taking a restrictive fare. The Sunday 6:10 looks like the sensible choice even though it costs more. I would rather not have Monday morning depend on a flight operating perfectly.

That gives you Sunday night in Chicago and removes the arrival-day risk. For Thursday, I see nonstop returns at 1:40, 4:25, 7:05, and 8:50 p.m. If the handoff ends around noon, the 1:40 departure is not realistic from downtown. The 4:25 could work if you leave the museum by about 1:30, while 7:05 is the safer choice if the lender runs into midafternoon.
The lender currently says Thursday morning, but that can mean anything from ten o'clock to after lunch. Is there a way to hold the Sunday flight with the 7:05 return without committing to it today?

Yes. I can place the Sunday 6:10 p.m. outbound and Thursday 7:05 p.m. return on a courtesy hold at the current $428 fare. The hold would expire at 8:00 p.m. Eastern tomorrow. It would not charge a card or issue a ticket. If the lender responds after the deadline, I would need to rebuild and reprice the itinerary.
Before you hold it, compare the 4:25 and 8:50 returns on that same outbound. I want to understand the tradeoff, not just the schedule.

With the Sunday 6:10 outbound, the 4:25 p.m. Thursday return totals $446 and lands in Atlanta at 7:20 p.m. The 7:05 return is $428 and arrives at 10:02 p.m. The 8:50 return is $412 and arrives at 11:47 p.m. All are nonstop and changeable with a fare difference. The 4:25 costs $18 more and requires an early museum departure; the 8:50 saves $16 but creates a very late arrival home.
Keep the 7:05 as the placeholder. It is the best middle ground. How much time should I allow from the museum to O'Hare on Thursday?

For a 7:05 p.m. domestic departure, I would plan to leave the museum by 3:45 p.m. That allows roughly 75 minutes for traffic, plus enough time for security and boarding. Leaving at 4:15 might still work in light traffic, but it would provide little protection from a slowdown on the Kennedy Expressway.
That is useful. If the handoff finishes at noon, I may switch to 4:25. If it runs beyond two, I will keep 7:05. Do either of those fares include seat selection?

Yes. Both standard economy options allow advance seat selection. On the held 7:05 itinerary, the outbound currently has several seats in rows 12 through 18, and the return has availability farther back in rows 21 through 27. Some preferred seats carry an added charge, but regular seats can be selected without one.
For this trip, put me in an aisle seat. I expect to be reviewing the condition notes in flight and may need to get into my bag more than once. Do not treat that as a change for later trips.

Understood. I will apply the aisle request only to this Chicago itinerary. Seat 14C is available on the outbound and 23D on the provisional return, both at no added cost. Because this is still a courtesy hold, the seats are requested but not guaranteed until the ticket is issued.
Use those for the hold. Also, does the outbound have Wi-Fi? I may need to answer installation emails before we land.

The scheduled aircraft lists Wi-Fi and in-seat power. Those amenities can change if the airline substitutes an aircraft, but they are shown for the current equipment. I can now place the itinerary and seat requests on hold without payment.
Go ahead. No charge and no ticket yet. I should hear from the lender by tomorrow afternoon.

The itinerary is on courtesy hold under reference CHI-4K82: Atlanta to Chicago on Sunday, October 19 at 6:10 p.m., and the provisional Chicago to Atlanta return on Thursday, October 23 at 7:05 p.m. The held fare is $428 round trip. Seats 14C and 23D are requested. Nothing has been charged, and no ticket has been issued. The hold expires tomorrow at 8:00 p.m. Eastern.
Good. When the lender replies, I will give you the actual end time. For now, note that 4:25 is only an option if I can leave the museum by 1:30; otherwise we stay with 7:05.

Noted. The 4:25 p.m. return remains an alternative only if you can leave the museum by 1:30 p.m.; otherwise the held 7:05 p.m. return is the working choice. I will not ticket or charge anything until you provide the lender's confirmed handoff time and authorize the purchase.
